September events – TOYOTA Motors, THT.cz and Zákupy corporate events

September was crazy right from the start, and the weather did its thing with our calendar. But that's nothing compared to the disaster that hit many people across the Czech Republic, and unfortunately the water didn't avoid us either (though only on a small scale). Events planned for the dates of the floods were of course all cancelled, and some others still being booked were cancelled too because of the clean-up.

At the start of the rains we practically only managed a corporate event for THT.cz, a manufacturer of fire and rescue vehicles. The event was indoors, so there was no problem, and we even managed to include a fire trailer, which they slightly modified for us. Vlasta's participation was in doubt because of a sprained ankle, but a bit of luck and his colleague Martin Šimůnek got him through the pain.

On this last weekend, when the worst has hopefully been averted / survived, we rode an exhibition for the guys from the Czech Olympic Committee and the partner of our Olympians – vehicle manufacturer TOYOTA in Kolín, right at their plant. Unfortunately the grassy area was still a bit waterlogged, so the exhibition had to be built so that the riders rode on the ground as little as possible. So we connected the stage to our obstacles and trailer. The ground was taken over by our Trial baby Marty Kabeláč, who showed adults and kids what a 7-year-old nipper can do. Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček then went wild on the obstacles in two shows. In Martin's case you could say he was breaking chains – because that's exactly what he managed when jumping from obstacle to obstacle. Luckily nothing was broken, and by some miracle he managed to walk away and host the rest of the show. During the second show the area in front of the obstacles dried out a bit, so we could hold a tape-jump competition with the spectators. The Trial part was part of a mini Olympic village where competitions took place as part of a sports day. Thanks for the invitation.

Right after the second show at Toyota we set off for two more exhibitions in Zákupy, where there was also a corporate event for employees. A smaller event, where Martin's sparring partner Mirek Brunclík was already waiting for us with a workshop. Martin fixed his bike, but Márty Kabeláč crashed on the concrete; after treatment he sat by the obstacles with an ice cream and kept his fingers crossed for us. The two shows with a competition for volunteers ran a bit long, and we got egged on to a tape jump of around 125–130 cm. 

We're sorting out the photos, so for now just a few quick ones in the gallery.
